decisions.reason: Source-only comments and metadata should not be judged as reader-facing prose.
A maintained source map makes scope and adaptation decisions reviewable without turning a living page into an automatic rules feed.
Wikitext, edit-summary, AfC, and policy-assurance patterns do not belong in general prose analysis unless a Wikipedia profile requests them.
A source revision prompts review. It cannot establish cross-genre usefulness or acceptable false-positive cost.
The measured composite score does not separate human and machine paragraphs, so project audits return editorial findings without an authorship score or classification.
Quotations, headings, code, and tables may preserve another speaker's language or serve non-prose functions. Profiles can mask them without shifting source offsets.
Negative pattern checks cannot define an author's voice. Profiles carry explicit hard rules, advisory rules, protected material, and positive craft guidance.
